name: ss
description: Socket statistics: shows listening ports, established connections, and their processes — the modern replacement for netstat.

flags.description: Numeric ports and addresses (no name resolution — faster).
Show the process owning each socket (needs root for other users' sockets).

examples.output:
Netid State  Local Address:Port   Process
tcp   LISTEN 0.0.0.0:22           sshd
udp   LISTEN 127.0.0.53:53         systemd-resolved
tcp   LISTEN 0.0.0.0:80           nginx
examples.explanation: THE command for "what is listening on my server": all TCP+UDP listening sockets with owning processes. 0.0.0.0 means exposed on all interfaces.

examples.output:
Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port  Peer Address:Port
0      0      192.168.1.20:22    203.0.113.7:51922
examples.explanation: Currently established TCP connections — who is connected to your services right now.
Filters connections with local (server) port 443 — live HTTPS traffic.

about: ss reads kernel socket state directly via netlink, making it faster and more detailed than netstat: it can filter by state, port, and even show socket memory queues (Recv-Q/Send-Q). A full Recv-Q means the application is not reading fast enough.
mistakes: Using netstat in new work — ss is maintained and faster.
Forgetting -n and waiting on slow reverse DNS lookups.
distroNotes: iproute2, standard on all modern distributions. BSD variants have different syntax.
